# Draft:Battle of Tewai

The Battle of Tewai was the final battle of the 18791880 Tabiteuean religious wars between Protestant and Anti-n-Tioba converts. It was fought in Tewai, South Tabiteuea, on September 15, 1880.
Most of South Tabiteuea adhered to Anti-n-Tioba, a Tabiteuean cult that syncretized Christian and indigenous practices. In 1880, having converted North Tabiteuea, Hawaiian Protestant missionaries W. B. Kapu and Henry Benjamin Nālimu began preaching a religious crusade against the south. During the battle, the followers of Anti-n-Tioba crowded around a cannon they salvaged in a shipwreck; they killed only one Protestant before they were encircled and killed.
The Protestant northerners continued the massacre across South Tabiteuea, killing hundreds of men, women, and children, and extinguishing Anti-n-Tioba. They split the conquered land among themselves. After an investigation by the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions, Nālimu was held largely responsible and removed from Tabiteuea in 1882. Kapu was allowed to remain on the atoll, continuing the theocracy he had built until his removal in 1892 for harassing Catholic convertsmany of which were former members of Anti-n-Tioba.
